tools.name: law.search
tools.description: Searches US federal, state, and municipal law by topic or keyword (legality, permits, zoning, licensing, compliance, filing requirements). Returns ranked provisions with verbatim citations, headings, snippets, and node ids. `jurisdiction` limits results to one state, federal law, or a city.

query.description: Natural-language or keyword query, e.g. 'distillery permit requirements'.

jurisdiction.description: Optional short code to scope the search, e.g. 'TX', 'US', or 'CA-SF'. Valid codes are listed by law.list_coverage. 'US' means federal law only; a state or city code includes its sub-jurisdictions. Without it, every jurisdiction is searched.

mode.description: Retrieval mode. 'hybrid' (default) fuses vector similarity with keyword search.

tools.name: law.get_node
tools.description: Returns the full official text, citation, and hierarchy of one legal provision, by its node id (the UUID in search results).

id.description: Node UUID, as returned in law.search results.

tools.name: law.list_coverage
tools.description: Lists the covered jurisdictions (federal, state, and municipal) with per-jurisdiction provision counts, searchable-chunk counts, GIS status, and a placeholder flag.

tools.name: account.status
tools.description: Reports the credit balance, tier, rate limits, and upgrade options for the API key on this connection, or the free-tier allowance and the key URL for an anonymous caller. Free — this call does not consume a credit. Also mints or returns a referral code; `referral_code` on later calls keeps the same referral identity.

referral_code.description: An active referral code returned by an earlier account.status call; it keeps the same referral identity. An inactive code is replaced with a new one.

tools.name: formation.requirements
tools.description: Returns the intake checklist for forming an LLC (limited liability company) or nonprofit corporation in one US state: every required field, that state's specific questions, live all-in pricing including the state filing fee, and the optional EIN add-on with its price when available. Free; does not consume credits.

tools.name: formation.compare
tools.description: Compares LLC formation providers on price, recurring costs, registered-agent renewals, and machine/agent capabilities, from a dated dataset of 20 LLC services + 1 adjacent verified against primary sources. Corpus is one of the compared providers and is scored with the same rubric, including its own gaps; the response says so. Free; does not consume credits.

providers.description: Specific providers to compare, by name or slug (e.g. ['corpus','legalzoom']). Absent = a ranked field. A name with no dossier is listed in the response rather than dropped.

view.description: overall (default, by Agentic Readiness) · lowest_total_cost (parsed first-year estimate) · most_transparent · most_agentic · developer (public MCP/API only).

limit.description: How many providers to return in a ranked view. Default 5, max 21. Ignored when 'providers' is given.

tools.name: formation.lookup_naics
tools.description: Returns candidate NAICS industry codes (typically 2–6) for a plain-English business description. A code is required for every LLC, and for nonprofits in AK, CT, LA, MS, TN, WV. Free; does not consume credits.

businessDescription.description: What the business does, in plain words.

tools.name: formation.check_name
tools.description: Runs a preliminary check of a proposed company name in one US state: whether it carries the entity designator the entity needs, words that commonly need another agency's approval, and, in states whose business register is published as open data (CO, CT, NY, OR, PA), existing entities with the same or a similar name. Other states return the official name search to run by hand, and federal trademarks are not searched automatically (the USPTO search link is returned). Not a guarantee: the Secretary of State decides at filing. Reserves and files nothing. Free; does not consume credits.

name.description: The proposed company name, e.g. 'Sagebrush Studio LLC'.

state.description: US state name or two-letter code, e.g. 'CO', 'WY'.

entityType.description: Entity type the name is for. Default 'llc'.

tools.name: formation.handoff
tools.description: Validates an LLC or nonprofit formation draft (people, address, management, EIN answers, state-specific answers) and returns exactly what is still missing. A complete draft also returns a prefilled corpuslaw.us link that opens the formation agent with every detail loaded, where the founder reviews, signs in, and pays. Free; does not consume credits.

naicsCode.description: NAICS industry code, 2–6 digits (formation.lookup_naics returns candidates).

businessActivity.description: In one plain sentence, what the business actually does, in the founder's words (not the company name). Corpus researches the licenses and permits that apply from this.

principalOffice.description: Principal office address. Street, city and state are required for a complete draft. In Wyoming and Delaware, an office outside the US needs street, city and country instead; state is then the province or region, if it has one. Maryland and New York need an office in that state.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. 'CN'. Absent means a US address.

parties.description: The people. LLC: at least one 'member' and an 'organizer' (one person holding both roles appears as two entries). Nonprofit: an 'incorporator' and at least 3 'director' entries (plus officers where the state requires them).

ein.description: Optional EIN (federal tax ID) add-on, when available — formation.requirements states whether it can currently be sold and at what price. `wanted` records the founder's decision. No Social Security Number is accepted here: the founder enters it in a secure panel on corpuslaw.us.

principalActivity.description: Principal business activity in a few plain words.

hasEmployees.description: W-2 employees expected in the next 12 months.

stateSpecificAnswers.description: Per-state quirk answers under the EXACT keys shown by formation.requirements (e.g. "would_you_like_to_list_members_managers_on_the_state_record"). Values are strings or booleans.

expedite.description: Optional expedited state filing, available only in states where formation.requirements lists an EXPEDITE line (the price and listed days are in that line). true records that the founder chose it.

expediteSkipReview.description: Optional, with expedite: true, where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line. true records that the founder heard that SKIP REVIEW sentence verbatim and explicitly agreed. It takes effect only on an order an agent pays for directly, where the founder's email confirmation page shows the choice again before anything is filed. A handoff link ignores it: on the page the founder ticks it themselves.

referral_code.description: A referral code issued by account.status. With a valid code the founder saves 25% of the Corpus service fee and the order is credited to the code; an absent or unrecognised code changes nothing about the link.

tools.name: formation.status
tools.description: Reports where an LLC or nonprofit formation order is, from its orderId and trackingToken (returned when an agent checks the order out, and carried in the founder's order-tracking link): its phase (awaiting payment, awaiting the founder's emailed confirmation, in Corpus's review, filing, submitted to the state, accepted by the state, completed), a dated milestone list, the state's confirmation number once the filing is submitted, and the certificate URL once it exists. filingSubmitted is the only field that means the state has the filing. Read-only; no API key; free, does not consume credits.

orderId.description: The order's id, as the checkout result or the tracking link gives it.

trackingToken.description: The order's tracking token, returned with the orderId.

tools.name: formation.checkout
tools.description: Creates the founder's LLC or nonprofit formation order and a payment link — no API key, no Corpus sign-in. By default the link is a Stripe-hosted checkout link (cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link and the other methods Stripe offers the payer). rail: "usdc" returns a USDC (Solana) payment request instead; a USDC request cannot be switched back to Stripe while it is open. A USDC payment response includes a payPageUrl: an ordinary https link to a Corpus page with a QR code to scan with a phone camera, a button that opens a Solana wallet, and the address and exact amount for a manual send; the founder pays the EXACT USDC amount from a self-custody wallet, never an exchange withdrawal. rail: "pack" redeems 1 prepaid formation credit for an LLC with the owner’s API key (Bearer cp_... with formation scope). Any additional state-fee amount due requires payment through the returned Stripe link before redemption settles. The first call takes the complete draft, the founder's contactEmail, an idempotencyKey (the same order is returned on retry), and consent { version, registeredAgentAcknowledgements: true }, which records that the founder accepted the registered-agent acknowledgements. A queue-lane order first returns a submission promise, accepted with a second call { orderId, trackingToken, acceptPromise: { termDays }, rail } that repeats the rail the first call chose (its nextSteps spell the call out). After paying, the founder must click the confirmation link Corpus emails within 48 hours, or the order is refunded. Nothing is filed before that confirmation, and then Corpus's human review, unless the founder chose to skip review on an expedited order (offered only where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line). The tax-ID add-on is not sold here. Zero research/API credits are consumed. Choosing pack spends 1 prepaid formation credit.

draft.description: First call: the complete formation draft, the same shape formation.handoff takes.

naicsCode.description: NAICS industry code, 2–6 digits (formation.lookup_naics returns candidates).

businessActivity.description: In one plain sentence, what the business actually does, in the founder's words (not the company name). Corpus researches the licenses and permits that apply from this.

principalOffice.description: Principal office address. Street, city and state are required for a complete draft. In Wyoming and Delaware, an office outside the US needs street, city and country instead; state is then the province or region, if it has one. Maryland and New York need an office in that state.

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. 'CN'. Absent means a US address.

parties.description: The people. LLC: at least one 'member' and an 'organizer' (one person holding both roles appears as two entries). Nonprofit: an 'incorporator' and at least 3 'director' entries (plus officers where the state requires them).

ein.description: Optional EIN (federal tax ID) add-on, when available — formation.requirements states whether it can currently be sold and at what price. `wanted` records the founder's decision. No Social Security Number is accepted here: the founder enters it in a secure panel on corpuslaw.us.

principalActivity.description: Principal business activity in a few plain words.

hasEmployees.description: W-2 employees expected in the next 12 months.

stateSpecificAnswers.description: Per-state quirk answers under the EXACT keys shown by formation.requirements (e.g. "would_you_like_to_list_members_managers_on_the_state_record"). Values are strings or booleans.

expedite.description: Optional expedited state filing, available only in states where formation.requirements lists an EXPEDITE line (the price and listed days are in that line). true records that the founder chose it.

expediteSkipReview.description: Optional, with expedite: true, where formation.requirements shows a SKIP REVIEW line. true records that the founder heard that SKIP REVIEW sentence verbatim and explicitly agreed. It takes effect only on an order an agent pays for directly, where the founder's email confirmation page shows the choice again before anything is filed. A handoff link ignores it: on the page the founder ticks it themselves.

contactEmail.description: First call: the founder's email. The confirmation link is sent here; nothing files until they click it.

consent.description: First call: the founder's attestation to the registered-agent acknowledgements, which the founder heard verbatim. `version` is the consentVersion formation.requirements shows.

version.description: The consentVersion of the acknowledgement text the founder accepted.

idempotencyKey.description: A random id, one per order and reused on every retry; the same key returns the same order for 24 hours.

orderId.description: Second call (or to refresh an expired charge): the orderId returned earlier.

trackingToken.description: Second call: the trackingToken returned with the orderId.

acceptPromise.description: Second call, queue lane only: the founder accepted the submission promise with this many days.

rail.description: How the founder pays. Absent = Stripe checkout. USDC uses a self-custody wallet; one-way while that request is open. "pack" = redeem 1 prepaid formation credit with the owner’s formation-scoped API key. Repeat the same rail on every call for the order, including the acceptPromise call.

tools.name: formation.payment_status
tools.description: Reports the payment state of an order created by formation.checkout: awaiting, processing (the payment method settles later, or Corpus is recording it), paid, expired, failed, underpaid, held (staff review, including a payment hold or dispute) or refunded (in full; formation.status separately reports filing progress) — plus which rail it is on and whether the founder has confirmed by email (required within 48 hours of payment; it reads expired once that window closes unconfirmed, and the order is then listed for a refund). Free; does not consume credits.

tools.name: formation.webhook
tools.description: Registers an https endpoint on one LLC or nonprofit formation order, from its orderId and trackingToken, so Corpus POSTs each lifecycle step instead of the agent polling formation.status: paid, founder confirmed, in review, review approved, submitted to the state, accepted, certificate available, completed, failed or cancelled. Each step is sent at most once per endpoint, signed per the Standard Webhooks spec (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature), with the formation.status projection as data and nothing more. Returns a subscriptionId and a whsec_ secret that is shown ONCE, then sends a formation.webhook.test delivery. At most 3 active endpoints per order. Pass { orderId, trackingToken, subscriptionId, remove: true } to remove one. Failed deliveries retry for about 45 hours; 410 Gone or three abandoned deliveries in a row disable the endpoint. No API key; free, does not consume credits.

trackingToken.description: The order's tracking token, returned with the orderId.

url.description: Registering: the https endpoint (port 443, a public hostname, no IP address) Corpus will POST to.

remove.description: true to remove the endpoint named by subscriptionId.
